comment:
* The X509V1CertImpl class is used as a conversion wrapper around
 * sun.security.x509.X509Cert certificates when running under JDK1.1.x.
 *
 * @author Jeff Nisewanger

methods.name: private static synchronized java.security.cert.CertificateFactory getFactory() throws java.security.cert.CertificateException
public byte[] getEncoded() throws CertificateEncodingException
methods.comment:
* Returns the encoded form of this certificate. It is
     * assumed that each certificate type would have only a single
     * form of encoding; for example, X.509 certificates would
     * be encoded as ASN.1 DER.

methods.name: public void verify(PublicKey key) throws CertificateException, NoSuchAlgorithmException, InvalidKeyException, NoSuchProviderException, SignatureException
methods.comment: * Throws an exception if the certificate was not signed using the * verification key provided. Successfully verifying a certificate * does not indicate that one should trust the entity which * it represents. * * @param key the public key used for verification.

methods.name: public void verify(PublicKey key, String sigProvider) throws CertificateException, NoSuchAlgorithmException, InvalidKeyException, NoSuchProviderException, SignatureException
methods.comment: * Throws an exception if the certificate was not signed using the * verification key provided. Successfully verifying a certificate * does not indicate that one should trust the entity which * it represents. * * @param key the public key used for verification. * @param sigProvider the name of the provider.

methods.name: public void checkValidity() throws CertificateExpiredException, CertificateNotYetValidException
methods.comment:
* Checks that the certificate is currently valid, i.e. the current
     * time is within the specified validity period.

methods.name: public void checkValidity(Date date) throws CertificateExpiredException, CertificateNotYetValidException
methods.comment:
* Checks that the specified date is within the certificate's
     * validity period, or basically if the certificate would be
     * valid at the specified date/time.
     *
     * @param date the Date to check against to see if this certificate
     *        is valid at that date/time.

methods.name: public String toString()
methods.comment:
* Returns a printable representation of the certificate.  This does not
     * contain all the information available to distinguish this from any
     * other certificate.  The certificate must be fully constructed
     * before this function may be called.

methods.name: public PublicKey getPublicKey()
methods.comment:
* Gets the publickey from this certificate.
     *
     * @return the publickey.

methods.name: public int getVersion()
methods.comment:
* Gets the version number from the certificate.
     *
     * @return the version number.

methods.name: public BigInteger getSerialNumber()
methods.comment:
* Gets the serial number from the certificate.
     *
     * @return the serial number.

methods.name: public Principal getSubjectDN()
methods.comment:
* Gets the subject distinguished name from the certificate.
     *
     * @return the subject name.
     * @exception CertificateException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: public Principal getIssuerDN()
methods.comment:
* Gets the issuer distinguished name from the certificate.
     *
     * @return the issuer name.
     * @exception CertificateException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: public Date getNotBefore()
methods.comment:
* Gets the notBefore date from the validity period of the certificate.
     *
     * @return the start date of the validity period.
     * @exception CertificateException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: public Date getNotAfter()
methods.comment:
* Gets the notAfter date from the validity period of the certificate.
     *
     * @return the end date of the validity period.
     * @exception CertificateException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: public String getSigAlgName()
methods.comment:
* Gets the signature algorithm name for the certificate
     * signature algorithm.
     * For example, the string "SHA1/DSA".
     *
     * @return the signature algorithm name.
     * @exception CertificateException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: public String getSigAlgOID()
methods.comment:
* Gets the signature algorithm OID string from the certificate.
     * For example, the string "1.2.840.10040.4.3"
     *
     * @return the signature algorithm oid string.
     * @exception CertificateException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: public byte[] getSigAlgParams()
methods.comment:
* Gets the DER encoded signature algorithm parameters from this
     * certificate's signature algorithm.
     *
     * @return the DER encoded signature algorithm parameters, or
     *         null if no parameters are present.
     * @exception CertificateException if a parsing error occurs.

methods.name: private synchronized void writeObject(ObjectOutputStream stream) throws IOException
private synchronized void readObject(ObjectInputStream stream) throws IOException
